feed.title: Frame & Light

bullets: Documentary frames carry the most weight when the photographer is closer than feels comfortable — proximity is the core operational principle.
Big distance lenses change how a photographer moves through a story, altering the tradeoffs between access and visual compression.
Framing matters because it tells you which tradeoffs you're making — the choice of frame is an explicit decision about what to include and exclude.
Color grading in documentary work is a point of changed opinion, suggesting that post-processing choices are revisable rather than fixed.
Editing workflow is where the conversation gets interesting — the layoff around data and workflow is what brings everything together.
A key heuristic is that documentary frames carry the most weight when the photographer is closer than feels comfortable; ignoring that leads to missing the point a year later.
The failure mode in documentary photography is ignoring the proximity principle, which results in work that doesn't hold up over time.
One actionable takeaway is to pick one of the discussed ideas and run it for two weeks — the rest is secondary.
